We're preparing for an internal team meeting (organized by someone named "Tash") about Sprint 3 priorities for "all things components" on the Zimmermann Salesforce PWA Kit project — specifically a proposed NEW approach to writing UI User Stories: moving from broad UI User Stories that encompass a whole group of components toward smaller, isolated, individually-specified component stories.

Context: this is a Confluence Cloud site, space key SFCC (https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/), root page "SFCC Migration" (id 241434627), roughly 146 pages. Known relevant pages from a prior research pass a few weeks ago (verify these are still current and accurately described — don't just trust this list blindly):
- 261750785 — Development Standards
- 261881857 — Component Override Strategy
- 258801666 — "04.2 Design Tracker" (tracks Figma sign-off status per feature area — as of a 2026-07-13 snapshot, Cart/Search/Checkout/Account/Wishlist/Gift Cards/Returns/Store Locator/Zimmerse were still Draft/In Review/Pending, while Homepage/PLP core grid/global nav+footer/most PDP components (images/gallery/product info/badges/colour-size/complete-the-look)/Payments-Notify-Me CTAs were Signed Off)
- 309690396 — "2.5 PI 1 Planning" (parent page) and 310050860 — "Dependencies" (child page)
- 256835585 — "Technical Solution Design – PWA"
- 268075023 — "1.5 Web Design (UX)"

Today's date is 2026-08-11. Please research Confluence (space SFCC) and report back on:

1. **Existing methodology docs**: Is there ANY existing page (draft or final) documenting a "component-based user story" methodology, a story-writing template/guideline, or a proposal for how to decompose UI work into stories? Use confluence_search with CQL/text for terms like "component-based", "user story", "story breakdown", "story template", "component story", "UI component", "ways of working", "story splitting", "INVEST". This meeting may be formalizing something that already exists as a draft somewhere — find it if it exists, and report its page ID, title, last-modified date, and author.

2. **Current Figma/design sign-off status**: Re-check the "04.2 Design Tracker" (258801666, or search for it if that ID is stale) for the CURRENT sign-off status per feature area — the info above is nearly a month stale. Focus especially on Cart, Search, PDP, PLP, since these were the features slated for "Sprint 3" work. Design sign-off status directly gates whether granular component stories are even buildable yet, so precision here matters.

3. **Component structure standards**: Check "Development Standards" (261750785) and "Component Override Strategy" (261881857) for what they currently say about component structure, granularity, or organization — do they already imply component-by-component story/build granularity, or something coarser (e.g., page-level)? Quote or closely paraphrase the relevant sections.

4. **Who is "Tash" and any Sprint 3 planning/retro content**: Try confluence_search_user for a name like Tasha/Natasha/Tash (she appears to be organizing this "ways of working" alignment meeting, likely a Scrum Master/PO/BA) — if found, search for pages she recently authored or updated. Also check "2.5 PI 1 Planning" (309690396) and its children (including 310050860 Dependencies) for anything about Sprint 3 scope, retro notes, or components specifically. Also search generally for any page titled or tagged with "Sprint 3".

5. **Component inventory**: Check whether there's a Confluence page inventorying the actual component library / design system — a list of all UI components expected to be built, atomic-design-style groupings, or similar. This would be directly useful for an "isolate stories per component" discussion since the team needs a shared inventory to cut isolated stories against.

Report back with page titles, IDs, last-modified dates/authors, and concrete content summaries/quotes relevant to each question above — I need specifics to act on and bring into a meeting, not generalities. Organize your report under the 5 numbered questions. This is read-only research — do not create, edit, or comment on any Confluence content. Keep the final report focused and well-structured; it will be read by another Claude session synthesizing a meeting-prep brief, not by an end user directly, so precision and specificity matter more than polish.

## Confluence Research Report — Sprint 3 "Component-Based User Stories" Meeting Prep

**Methodology note:** This Confluence MCP tool returns blank `created`/`updated` fields on every `get_page`/`get_page_history` call regardless of page (confirmed across ~15 pages) — a tool limitation, not a data gap. Where an exact date matters, I've substituted: (a) dates written into the page content itself, (b) the page's `version` number as a recency proxy, or (c) `lastModified >=` CQL boundary probes I ran to bracket the true last-edit date. These are flagged inline. No content was created, edited, or commented on.

---

### 1. Existing methodology docs — YES, found, and it's brand new

Two pages, added as the newest children under the "04 Business Documentation" family (id 244252674, siblings 04.0–04.6), sitting **after** 04.6 Consent Management — i.e., the most recently added pages in that entire numbered series:

- **"04.7 Component Inventory"** — id `400195591`, version 13.
- **"04.71 Writing User Stories for Components"** — id `400195600`, version 2, the sole child of 04.7.

**04.71 is the methodology doc itself.** Full text defines exactly the split the meeting is about:
- **Level 1 — Component epics**: "the build story for each individual component... variants and configurations, accessibility requirements, and any error or empty states." Splits further by component type: **PWA Kit only** (Button, Textfield, Dropdown, Cart Item — "Write one story, in the PWA Kit epic only") vs. **Contentful + PWA Kit** (Banner, Editorial Cards, Footer, Navigation — "Write two stories: one in the Contentful epic... one in the PWA Kit epic").
- **Level 2 — Page epics**: "the experience story for a specific page (e.g. PDP, PLP, Checkout)... describe how components work together... written from the customer's perspective... should not repeat the component build detail from Level 1."
- Includes a quick-reference table (Level / Epic / Focus / Written-from-perspective).

Both pages have **zero comments** (`confluence_get_comments` returned `[]` for both) — not yet socialized with the wider team. Both are confirmed freshly edited: a `lastModified >= "2026-08-10"` probe matched on both IDs, and 04.7's own content contains inline dates "confirmed by Dennis 2026-08-10" and "Sprint 3 for User Story Writing 2026-08-11 - 2026-08-24" (2026-08-11 is today). Author identity is not retrievable via this tool (blank metadata on both), but the timing makes it near-certain this was assembled in the last 1–2 days, directly ahead of the meeting — this is very likely the exact thing being formalized.

**Distinct, older, non-conflicting doc found too:** "Creating User Stories with Claude" (id `274137093`, version 11, self-dated "Last updated: July 2026") — a BA guide for the *mechanics* of drafting/creating Jira stories via Claude (custom fields, Given/When/Then AC format, labels like `HPC-034;Custom;Squad-A`, FE/BE splitting rule, bulk creation). It never addresses component-vs-page epic granularity, and there is **no cross-link** in either direction between it and 04.71. Worth flagging as a doc-consolidation opportunity for the meeting.

Also checked and confirmed silent on this topic: "Definition of Ready" (313589763, v1), "Story Workflow" (247922696, v12), "2.6 Ways of Working" (313458697, v3 — owned by the Scrum Master, "reviewed at the end of each PI," changes are "raised in the Sprint Retrospective"). No hits anywhere in the space for "INVEST," "story splitting," or "story template" as search terms; no hits for "component-based" or "component story" other than 04.7/04.71 themselves.

---

### 2. Design/Figma sign-off status — current, and materially different from the month-old snapshot in places

**04.2 Design Tracker (id `258801666`, version 44)** — still exists, same title. Pinned its true last-edit date via binary search on `lastModified`: matched `>= "2026-07-13"`, empty on `>= "2026-07-14"` and `>= "2026-08-01"`. **Conclusion: last edited exactly 13 July 2026 — untouched for 29 days as of today (11 Aug).** The page's own intro text is stale too ("Phase 2 designs are... planned to be done by mid-July 2026" — already passed). This means your existing 2026-07-13 snapshot is **not** outdated relative to this specific page — nothing has changed on it since.

Per area (Design Status | Zimmermann Sign-off):
- **Cart & Inventory (Sprint 2)**: Mini-Cart — Pending/Pending. Full Cart Page — Pending/Pending. **Nothing signed off.**
- **Search & Recommendations (Sprint 2)**: Search Input & Autocomplete, Search Results & Zero-Results, Recommendation Carousels — all Pending/Pending. **Nothing signed off.**
- **PLP (Sprint 1-2)**: Product Tile, Quick Add & Wishlist Popovers, Breadcrumb navigation, Filter/Sort/View More, Editorial & Content Blocks — **all five rows Pending/Pending.** ⚠️ **This contradicts the prior research pass's claim that "PLP core grid" was Signed Off** — current live content shows zero PLP sign-off. Flag this explicitly and verify live before the meeting; either the earlier note was wrong or conflated something else.
- **PDP (Sprint 1-2)**: Signed off — Images, Image Gallery, Product Info, Badges, Colour & Size Selection, Complete the Look. Done-but-signoff-Pending — Accordions, Need Assistance. Fully Pending both — Measmerize, Price & Stock, More from the Edit, Recommended for You, Recently Viewed, SEO section. **Anomaly worth a live check**: "Primary CTAs" shows Design Status text "PENDING" but colour-flagged green, sign-off "SIGNED OFF" — yet a 13-07 note says the Notify Me modal design was updated afterward ("misses customer name fields + marketing comms checkbox & success screen — design updated"), i.e. the signed-off state may now be stale relative to the actual Figma file.

**Separately — and this is the more actionable tracker for Sprint 3 — the new 04.7 Component Inventory is current as of yesterday (10 Aug)** and tracks sign-off at the atomic UI-kit level instead of the page/feature level:
- Mostly **✅ Done (confirmed by Dennis 2026-08-10)**, already tagged "Sprint 3 for User Story Writing": Banner+Pause/Play, Button, Icon Button, Footer+Footer Item/Footer Textfield/Icons, Disclaimer, Textfield, Dropdown, Link, Logo Masthead, Navigation, Product Card Base+Image Carousel/Wishlist Icon, Product Cards with Lookbook, Recently Viewed.

**Net for the meeting:** two trackers, different granularity, different currency (04.2 stalled since 13 Jul; 04.7 live as of 10 Aug). Page-level (Level 2) epics for Cart/Search/PLP are blocked — the **Definition of Ready** (id `313589763`) states plainly: "Stories with UI components are not Ready without approved designs." But isolated Level-1 PWA-Kit-only component stories (Button, Dropdown, Textfield, Banner, Footer, etc.) look buildable now per 04.7, independent of their parent pages' unsigned-off status.

### 3. Component structure standards — silent on story granularity, but the code structure already implies component-level units

Full-text review confirms **neither mentions "user story," "epic," or story-writing granularity anywhere.**
- They do already imply component-level (not page-level) *build* granularity: "New custom components go under `overrides/app/components/custom/`" with each getting `index.tsx` + required `index.stories.tsx` + conditional `index.test.ts`; "Every component exported from `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/` must have a `.stories.tsx` file." This 1-folder-per-component structure lines up naturally with 04.71's "one component epic per component" — the codebase's unit of organisation already matches the proposed unit of story-writing.
- **No cross-links exist** between these two docs and 04.7/04.71 in either direction — another documentation-consolidation opportunity to raise.

---

### 4. Who is "Tash," and Sprint 3 content

**"Tash" = Natasha Lay, ACN (Accenture) Delivery Lead, Accenture Onshore, Sydney.** Confirmed via **"1.2 Team Overview"** (id `261586947`, v7), Project Executive Council table: `ACN Delivery Lead | Izzy Chaloner / Tash Lay | Accenture Onshore | Sydney` (a shared/paired row with Izzy Chaloner). She is **not** the Scrum Master/PO/BA you hypothesized — Hazel Cacalda (Accenture Offshore) holds Scrum Master for *both* squads (per Team Overview and both Sprint 3 pages below). **Sprint 3 tracking pages** (not in your original list — found via direct title search): **"A - Sprint 3"** (id `396656658`, v3) and **"B - Sprint 3"** (id `396656649`, v5).
